description: Execute a SQL query against an IRIS namespace and return column names and row data. Supports parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection. Use maxRows to limit result set size (default: 1000). An operator may set IRIS_SQL_MAX_ROWS (a ceiling on the number of rows returned — the response carries rowsCapped: true when it clamps the caller's request; it bounds the returned row count post-fetch, not the server-side result set or transfer) and/or IRIS_SQL_TIMEOUT (per-request timeout in seconds) as environment variables; both are opt-in and unset by default. Safety controls: readOnly (default: false) runs only queries (SELECT) and refuses every other statement, CALL included, with SQL_READ_ONLY; maxRowsAffected (default: no cap) is a ceiling on the rows an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE may change; a statement that changes more is rolled back and refused with SQL_ROWS_AFFECTED_CAP, and under a cap only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE run, because those are the statements whose affected rows IRIS counts (the count is the statement's own row count: rows that triggers, cascades or functions change are not counted, and a SELECT is not bounded by it), and an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE whose text contains the %NOJOURN token (a comment or a string counts) is refused with SQL_ROWS_AFFECTED_CAP before it runs under a cap, because it turns journaling off and the rollback could not undo it; countOnly (default: false) returns only totalCount, the number of rows a SELECT returns, and transfers no rows. An operator may set IRIS_SQL_READ_ONLY=true (every call is read-only; unset by default) and IRIS_SQL_MAX_ROWS_AFFECTED (a non-negative integer ceiling no call can raise; unset by default); a call can only tighten them, and the result carries readOnlyForced or maxRowsAffectedCapped when one of them applied. An INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE result carries rowsAffected (IRIS reports -1 for TRUNCATE TABLE). Read-only mode is statement-level read-only, not side-effect-free: the statement runs inside a transaction that is always rolled back. The transaction undoes SQL changes and journaled global sets made by functions and triggers, but not $INCREMENT/$SEQUENCE counters (row ID counters included), process-private or IRISTEMP globals, changes made with %NOJOURN by a function, procedure or trigger the statement runs, work that parallel query worker processes do (%PARALLEL), JOB or device output, other external effects, or a function, procedure or trigger that starts, commits or rolls back a transaction (reported as an error when the transaction level the tool opened has changed, which a commit followed by a new TSTART does not show; some changes may be saved). A capped statement that is rolled back leaves the same effects. Under the read-only governance preset this tool is blocked: use iris_sql_query to run queries.

countOnly.description: Return only totalCount, the number of rows a SELECT returns, and transfer no rows (default: false)

maxRows.description: Maximum number of rows to return as an integer (default: 1000)

maxRowsAffected.description: Roll back and refuse an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE that changes more than this many rows; 0 is a dry count (default: no cap; IRIS_SQL_MAX_ROWS_AFFECTED sets a ceiling this cannot raise). Under a cap only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE run, and an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE whose text contains the %NOJOURN token is refused.

parameters.description: Parameterized query values as a JSON array matching ? placeholders in the query (e.g., ["MyApp."] for a single parameter)

query.description: SQL query to execute (e.g., 'SELECT Name FROM %Dictionary.ClassDefinition WHERE Name %STARTSWITH ?')

readOnly.description: Run only queries (SELECT) and refuse any other statement before it runs (default: false; IRIS_SQL_READ_ONLY=true forces it on)

server.description: Named server profile to target for this call (from `IRIS_PROFILES`). Omit to use the default server.

name: iris_sql_execute
title: Execute SQL
